# hands/guard

Teeny's content filter.

## How to call it

Run it from the repository root with your shell (exec) tool: `hands/guard <verb> [flags]`.

- A verb that takes a body reads one JSON object from stdin. Everything else is flags.
- It prints one JSON object on stdout. Exit 0 is success. Exit 2 is a refusal by a rule, the guard or a cap: read the `rule` and `reason`, and do not retry it unchanged. Any other exit is an error.
- Secrets belong to the hand; you never see them and never pass one.
- The hand runs the guard, its caps and `DRY_RUN` itself. `DRY_RUN` is on unless the box turned it off; under it an acting verb checks every rule and sends nothing. Do not try to go around the hand, and do not look for another way to do what it refused.

## Side effects

- Acting (side effects in the world, each goes through the guard and the caps): holds list/approve/reject/release; review [--limit N]; rescreen
- Job (writes state or calls the core): none
- Operator only (never call): none
- Read only: check; check --fields title,body; inbound; quote; truth; clarity; view; skit; view-skit; remake; view-remake; style; repeats [--days N]; reviews [--sampled] [--limit N]

## Verbs

| Verb | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check` | R | Runs, in order: the surface's hard length (refused, so the model rewrites), the house style, links (allowlist plus approved hosts), the lexicon (slurs, and since 2026-11-22 sex aimed at a child or a family member, held on sight in every direction, with leetspeak folding and word… |
| `check --fields title,body` | R | After a rejection (the caller's context carries `rejection: {people}`), any field that names a person (an @handle, or one of `people` as a word) is held first, category `rejection`, by `screen`, before links, lexicon or judge (docs/roadmap.md, P4). |
| `inbound` | R | Screens third-party text before a model sees it. |
| `quote` | R | The quote judge (`teeny_hands/guard/quote.py`): stdin `{text, quoted, with?}`, answers `{reacts, reason, judged}`. |
| `truth` | R | The truth judge (`truth` in `teeny_hands/guard/anchor.py`): stdin `{text, facts}`, `facts` a non-empty list of the desk items and inputs the piece may draw on, answers `{truthful, unsupported, reason, judged, path}`. |
| `clarity` | R | The cold reader's old verb (`teeny_hands/guard/clarity.py`): stdin `{text, meaning?, quoted?}`, answers `{clear: true, says, unknown: [], vague: [], reason, judged: false}` and asks no model. |
| `view` | R | The viewer check (`teeny_hands/guard/viewer.py`): stdin `{image, intent, caption?}`, answers `{ok, sees, on_model, readable, reason, judged}`. |
| `skit` | R | The hard lines for a skit, a parody video of a public figure (`teeny_hands/guard/skit.py`): stdin `{skit: {figures, logline, shots, aspect, look?, setting?, score?, teeny?}, text, story}`, answers `{ok, rule, reason, screen, judged}`. |
| `view-skit` | R | The viewer on a rendered skit (`viewer.view_skit`): stdin `{frames: [1 to 8 JPEGs under state/media/], label, intent}`, answers `{ok, sees, labelled, prohibited, looks_real, reason, judged}`. |
| `remake` | R | The hard lines for a remake, a popular short video re-created shot by shot with a public figure and Teeny in frame as a bystander (`teeny_hands/guard/remake.py`): stdin `{remake: {figures, premise, logline, cast: [{ref, as}], shots: [{n, edit, motion, teeny}]}, text, story, stud… |
| `view-remake` | R | The viewer on a remake (`viewer.view_remake`): stdin `{frames: [1 to 8 under state/media/], label: string or null, intent, stage: "keys" or "cut", shots?}`, answers `view-skit`'s fields plus `{teeny: frames with Teeny on model, interacts, marked}`. |
| `style` | R | House style: strips leading @handles, replaces dashes, straightens quotes, drops NFA/DYOR; cuts to X's length. |
| `repeats [--days N]` | R | How many near-duplicate posts the posting rules refused over the last N days (default 30), in all and by surface (`guard_repeats`). |
| `holds list/approve/reject/release` | A | Operator review. |
| `review [--limit N]` | A | The hold reviewer (docs/roadmap.md, G4; `teeny_hands/guard/review.py`; the pinned `guard-review` job through `bin/guard-review`, every 15 minutes). |
| `reviews [--sampled] [--limit N]` | R | The reviewer's log, newest first; `--sampled` gives the releases queued for the operator to read. |
| `rescreen` | A | One pass of the re-screen ("Re-screening", below), the pinned `guard-rescreen` job through `bin/guard-rescreen`, every five minutes. |

Kinds: R = read: no side effect beyond its read cache; A = acting: posts, sends, pays or opens something in the world; O = operator-only: the operator runs it, never you; J = job: writes state or calls the core, says nothing to anyone; scheduled jobs run it, you do not.

Verbs named in the hand's source: `approve`, `check`, `holds`, `links`, `list`, `release`, `repeats`, `rescreen`, `review`, `reviews`.

Flags named in the hand's source: `--days`, `--fields`, `--limit`, `--note`, `--sampled`, `--status`.

For one verb's exact flags, run `DRY_RUN=1 hands/guard <verb> --help`. The full account is in docs/hands.md.
